meta.scope: Iran Batch 3 — Fiscal (budget, oil revenues, subsidies), exchange-rate regime, and China trade linkage.

candidates.title: State budget revenue and expenditure statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Finance / related
candidates.description: Official and reported state budget figures covering oil and non-oil revenues, current and capital expenditure, and overall fiscal balance. Oil-revenue shortfalls relative to budget assumptions are a recurring feature under sanctions.

candidates.title: Targeted subsidies and energy-subsidy framing
candidates.description: Policy and statistical framing of the large subsidy system (energy, essential goods, cash transfers). Subsidy reform attempts interact tightly with inflation, exchange-rate policy and fiscal sustainability.
candidates.notes: High-centrality domestic policy node linking fiscal, energy and welfare.

candidates.title: Exchange-rate regime and parallel-market statistics
candidates.publisher: Central Bank of Iran / parallel-market trackers
candidates.description: Official and parallel-market exchange rates for the rial. Multiple rate systems and large gaps between official/preferential and free-market rates are a persistent feature under sanctions and high inflation.
candidates.notes: Critical price and external-constraint node. Parallel-market premium is a key signal.

candidates.title: Iran–China merchandise trade and oil sales statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from customs, CBI and shipping sources
candidates.description: Bilateral trade with China, with particular emphasis on oil and petrochemical exports. China is the dominant remaining large-scale buyer of Iranian crude under sanctions; non-oil trade is also significant.
candidates.notes: Primary bilateral trade corridor under sanctions. China is the key residual oil market.

candidates.title: Iran fiscal–exchange–China densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from fiscal, CBI and trade sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding state budget, targeted subsidies, exchange-rate/parallel-market statistics, and Iran–China trade/oil sales into a coherent fiscal–monetary–external layer that interacts tightly with the oil and sanctions nodes from Batch 2.
referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Oil, sanctions, CPI and BOP series from earlier batches
candidates.notes: Integrating node for the fiscal and external densification pass.
